speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with sudden-onset vertigo; to begin our evaluation, have you experienced any severe headache, double vision, or difficulty speaking alongside the spinning sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is good news regarding your cranial nerves, as the brief duration of your symptoms points toward a peripheral cause. Given your age and the specific nature of the episode, have you noticed any recent episodes of hearing loss, tinnitus (ringing in the ear), or a feeling of fullness in the affected ear?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The brief, three-minute duration of your vertigo is highly characteristic of benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), but we must rule out other causes. Have you noticed any recent falls, head trauma, or specific positions that triggered the spinning sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the duration was only three minutes, it is likely Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). To confirm this, have you noticed that your dizziness specifically occurs when you roll over in bed or look up?

REQUEST TEST: Dix_Hallpike_Manoeuver

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient's symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
